source: Not a book section. The four-part shape of a game (goal, score, loss, restart) follows CodeHS's project modules in Introduction to Game Design, where each project is built in setup/mechanics/challenge steps. Structure only: no CodeHS text, problems or code is copied.

lessons.title: Plan, and from scene to game
lessons.objective: Students will be able to plan a game as parts and remembered values, name the four things that turn a physics scene into a game, and build a table with a goal on it.

lessons.title: Scoring an event
lessons.objective: Students will be able to explain why a collision fires every frame, and score a hit exactly once by remembering the frame before.

lessons.title: Losing and restarting
lessons.objective: Students will be able to hold a game's state in a variable and use it to end and restart a game.

lessons.title: Playtest, and make it yours
lessons.objective: Students will be able to playtest their own game, link what they saw to their code, and extend it with a rule of their own.

lessons.title: A sound on a hit
lessons.objective: Students will be able to load a sound once in setup(), play it once per hit by putting .play() inside the same edge check that scores, and explain why a game can stay silent until the first click.
